# Facilitator Guide — AI FinOps

Slides: `slides/slides.md`. Demos: `demos/`. Exercise sheets: `exercises.md`. Every demo runs offline; start times assume 09:30.

**One week before:** run `python demos/run_all.py`. Confirm room, projector, one laptop per pair, Wi-Fi. Print exercises and handouts.

## Day 1

| Time | Segment | What you do and say |
|---|---|---|
| 09:30 | Welcome | Outcomes on the first slide. Ask each table for the one question they want answered; write them on the flipchart. |
| 09:40 | **Module 1 — Unit economics** | Teach: cost per request / task / user, attribution. |
| 10:01 | Demo 1 | **Run `python demos/01_unit_economics.py`** — a month of usage logs turned into cost per request, per resolved task and per active user, attributed by feature and team, with the margin check. Close with: *“The bill is per token. The business runs per task. FinOps is the translation.”* |
| 10:16 | Lab 1 | Cost model — see `exercises.md`. Walk the room; collect one result per table. |
| 10:40 | **Module 2 — Controls** | Teach: prompt caching, routing, batch, quantisation, output limits, agent caps. |
| 11:27 | Break |  |
| 11:42 | Demo 2 | **Run `python demos/02_apply_three_controls.py`** — six cost controls applied one at a time to the same workload, showing the saving, the quality risk and the effort of each. Close with: *“Do the free controls first: cache, trim, cap the output. Routing is the big one, and the only one that needs an eval suite.”* |
| 12:07 | Lab 2 | Apply three controls — see `exercises.md`. Walk the room; collect one result per table. |
| 12:55 | Lunch |  |
| 13:40 | **Module 3 — Reporting** | Teach: dashboards, alerts, budget governance. |
| 14:01 | Demo 3 | **Run `python demos/03_dashboard_and_budget_alerts.py`** — a month-to-date spend view with forecast, budget burn alerts by team, anomaly detection on cost per request and the monthly governance ritual. Close with: *“A budget alert on day 21 is a conversation. An invoice on day 35 is an incident.”* |
| 14:16 | Lab 3 | Dashboard spec — see `exercises.md`. Walk the room; collect one result per table. |
| 14:40 | Close | Assessment: FinOps plan for one system. Return to the flipchart questions — tick the ones answered. |

## If short on time

Keep every demo; shorten the teaching before it. Cut labs to a paired discussion of the lab question rather than dropping them. Never cut the close.

## What can go wrong

- **A demo fails on the day** — you ran `run_all.py` last week, so it is the environment: `pip install -r requirements.txt`, then re-run. Screenshots of each output live in nobody's folder: take them after your dry run.
- **No projector / terminal too small** — open `/demos` in a browser and run the same demo from the *Course labs* section.
- **The room has no laptops** — run labs as table discussions using the printed exercise sheet; you run the script and change the inputs they call out.
